title: Food Safety, Eating Habits, Sodium Intake, and Hypertension: An Overview in Brazil
content: In the last decades, with the increase in Brazilian urbanization and decrease in the time of food preparation, there was a change in eating habits, a reduction in food quality and the increase in some diseases. Hypertension is responsible for most of premature deaths in the world, having as its main cause the excessive amount of sodium consumption. In this context, this study aims to describe an overview of eating habits, labelling, sodium intake, and hypertension in Brazil. A literature review  was carried out using studies on this subject to improve the current understanding of this disease, labelling, sodium intake, and also the change in eating habits. In July 2024, five mayonnaise brands, five cheese brands, and five bread brands were bought in a local supermarket to evaluate the sodium concentration on the labels according to the Brazilian law. Some sodium labels analyzed were not in compliance with the country legislation. The results of this study showed the importance of improving food safety in the food chain. Research shows the need for the promotion of healthy eating patterns and physical activity, the increase in fruit and vegetable consumption, as well as improvements in food education. The incorrect values of sodium in the food label can put in risk the health of population mainly people with hypertension.
